articles.title: Denis Villeneuve Reveals the 1 James Bond Quality He Looked For, And It's the Opposite of Pattinson's Batman
articles.summary: News that Robert Pattinson will be the new James Bond shook Hollywood yesterday, but it shouldn't have, considering he just made Dune: Part 3 with director Denis Villeneuve. Announced as the director behind the new Bond movie over a year ago, the Oscar-nominated director has put his mark on multiple franchises, with the chance to […]
articles.content:
Speaking in an interview with GQ ( clearly recorded a few weeks before the casting was finalized ), Denis Villeneuve was asked what makes a good Bond to him, revealing qualities and traits that are easy to see applying to Robert Pattinson, but including one that stands in stark contrast to the star's other major character, Batman . “A first quality is that I need to believe that this man is a killer, because more than a spy, Bond is an assassin, and I need that kind of strength. I need that kind of anger deep in the eyes. It's not everybody who has that.” Villeneuve is right about these Bond qualities, but it's quite funny to think about how they describe the same person playing the famously anti-killing DC superhero.

The eyes of a killer, and the believability that he could kill with ease, were just some of the traits that Villeneuve spotlighted as what he sought after in a new Bond. He further added that an “unapologetic panache” that leads to an entire room gravitating around him was another, and that's on top of, what else, a sensuality.

He continued, “Someone who expresses some kind of pleasure, someone who has width, sometimes who has dark humor, sometimes that has pleasure in being in deep sh-t, someone who is not afraid to put his hand in the mud. I need someone that is strong, muscular, someone that is a force, and someone, of course, who has a deep intelligence in the eyes, someone that is always ahead of us.” Villeneuve added, “And I have good ideas,” which means he could have been thinking about Pattinson all along.

Without even a title or a release date for Denis Villeneuve's James Bond, we still don't really know what to expect from the film. That said, he broke down what he loves about the series as well, which could very well offer clues about what will be his priorities in bringing a new take on the character to the big screen.

“It's a character that I grew up with that I adore. I adore James Bond. I adore Sean Connery, the Sean Connery years, the birth of James Bond, his panache, his drive, his charisma, his unapologetic way of living, the strength, what it says, good and bad, about masculinity. There's something about James Bond that deeply inspires me….Every time I'm thinking about James Bond, there's electricity that goes into my veins; it's the electricity of pleasure.”

No release date has been set for Denis Villeneuve's James Bond, but with the release of Dune: Part 3 happening in just a few weeks (ahead of what we can only assume will be a long awards season push for the sequel), it's possible that production on the movie could finally happen next year. Should it happen, James Bond could return to theaters as soon as 2028, which would mark the longest gap between films in the series since it began back in 1962. If a 2028 release date is confirmed, it would give Robert Pattinson even more distinction, not only as the first actor to play Batman AND James Bond, but to star as the characters in teh same year.

articles.title: Emma Chamberlain Returning to YouTube With Original Series 'What Are You Waiting For?' (Exclusive)
articles.summary: The veteran creator is ditching the vlog format for a docuseries concept.
articles.content:
One of YouTube ‘s original superstars is planning a major comeback to the platform.

Emma Chamberlain, whose vlogs on the platform propelled her to stardom (she has more than 12 million followers there), is launching a new show on YouTube next year, The Hollywood Reporter has learned.

Chamberlain will launch the docuseries What Are You Waiting For? in which she explores some of New York's most popular lines, and the people waiting in them.

" What Are You Waiting For? on the surface is about people who voluntarily wait in lines for stuff set in New York City, a phenomenon that I personally don't understand but seek to understand, and along the way I discover much more about humanity than I ever could have expected,” Chamberlain says. “The experience of making this was unlike anything I have ever done and has profoundly changed me as a person, talking to strangers all day, working with a crew of unbelievably talented people, and making something bigger than I have ever made before, I feel the next chapter of my life coming to fruition, and I am deeply inspired and grateful."

The show is being produced in partnership with Amplify Pictures, underscoring how content on YouTube is professionalizing and becoming more ambitious. In fact, Chamberlain is debuting the new concept at a YouTube Creator Premieres event in Los Angeles Tuesday evening, with Wesley Yang and Aryna Sabalenka also making appearances.

It's also a coup for the platform, which has been trying to entice top creators to develop shows and programming primarily for itself at a moment when there are a number of competitors pursuing deals with top talent.

"After deciding to take a hiatus from my podcast, I spent the next few months trying to figure out what I wanted to create next,” Chamberlain says. “The answer wasn't obvious at first, but I knew for sure that I wanted to make something for YouTube. From entertaining me as a child to allowing me to build a career as an adult, it was a no-brainer that whatever I make next had to go on YouTube.”

“Working with a TV studio to create YouTube content is a full 180 from what I have done in the past, producing everything myself with very little help, but I knew this was crucial,” she added. “I met with Joe Lewis and Amplify Pictures and explained a little idea I had for a docuseries. To my surprise, they loved it and wanted to make it with me.”

articles.title: Naruto's Creator Has the Chance to Redeem Himself From His Biggest Failure
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Pierrot Masashi Kishimoto is returning with a new Naruto sequel, and it might finally make fans forget about the huge disaster Samurai 8: The Tale of Hachimaru was. As the creator of one of the most iconic Shonen series of all time, there's no denying Kishimoto is a beloved manga creator known for his exceptional art […]
articles.content:
However, the new manga, Naruto: Shadow Rising , could instead do the opposite. The teaser revealed that the series will focus on the period after the events of Shippuden and before Naruto became Hokage. This suggests that the series will follow Naruto’s journey toward becoming Hokage, advancing through the ranks, and possibly going on missions alongside Sakura and his other teammate, Sasuke, with Team 7 back on missions under Kakashi’s guidance. While these events could be featured, the new manga’s main focus could actually be bridging the gap between Naruto and the next generation, and the teaser also hints that it will focus on Boruto and the next generation.

Naruto: Shadow Rising features Kishimoto returning with a new manga story, but it’s yet to be revealed what kind of shape this new story will take. It could be a single one-shot story focusing on a time Naruto and Sasuke fought before Naruto became the Hokage ( something that was not shown during the events of the main series ), or it could be a miniseries with multiple chapters set to release much like other sequels of its kind like Jujutsu Kaisen Modulo . But there are still many other questions surrounding this return that just keep popping up.

Naruto Shadow Rising seems to take place after the original series, but before the events of the Boruto: Naruto Next Generations sequel . It’s kind of like Dragon Ball Super’ s situation where it can’t do too much without interfering with the canon of its future events seen in the sequel, but that franchise has gone on for so long that it’s basically become its own timeline. That could be the case with this manga return, or it could end after a single chapter. We’ll find out soon enough when it takes the stage during Jump Festa 2027 later this year.

The teaser for Naruto: Shadow Rising now hints that the manga could focus on filling this gap. Specifically, the new illustrations showcase Naruto’s Hokage statue being built and Sarada with her newborn daughter. This suggests that the manga will explore events surrounding the period when Naruto and other original characters, including Sasuke and Shikamaru, started having children. With Naruto’s priorities shifting from becoming Hokage for his own sake to caring for others, particularly the next generation, this manga could explore that transition. It could focus on Naruto and his companions navigating parenthood as they work to secure a better future for the next generation.

It feels like it wasn’t long ago since news went live about Samurai 8, but its end is already here. A few years back saw artist Masashi Kishimoto return to work following his iconic run with Naruto , and Samurai 8 was his big prize. The sci-fi series is one which Kishimoto had been wanting to do for years, and his newfound freedom gave him a chance to pursue the project. But just after a year of being published, the manga has come to an end .

Fans had a lot of emotions about the manga, and its ending has sparked some passionate reactions. While some are glad to be rid of the series, others are far more frustrated by the early ending. Weekly Shonen Jump isn’t afraid to axe underperforming series , and Samurai 8 hasn’t done well in sales so far. Japanese audiences never caught onto the sci-fi series, but those who did read the manga are sad to see all its potential lost.

This abrupt end marks the final chapter of Samurai 8 and its legacy . There is no word on whether Kishimoto or Okubo have projects lined up in the wake of this finale. For the former, he could always circle back to Boruto: Naruto Next Generations , but Kishimoto certainly deserves a break if he wants one. And if that is the case, fans are more than ready to give him and Okubo all the rest they need to launch a comeback.

Do you think Masashi Kishimoto can redeem himself with this sequel after Samurai 8 ‘s cancellation? What are your expectations for Naruto: Shadow Rising ? Share your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: Ron Howard Reveals His Only Condition for Making The Grinch 2: “Jim & I Are Aligned On One Thing”
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Universal Ron Howard's 2000 classic Christmas movie How the Grinch Stole Christmas currently has a sequel in development, but he and the Grinch star Jim Carrey are only moving forward on one condition. The holiday season is currently upon us, which means a host of all-time favorite titles are making the rounds once again, from Home […]
articles.content:
It was therefore thrilling to learn that the movie is getting a sequel , although that's also quite a daunting task, considering that How the Grinch Stole Christmas has been beloved for more than 25 years. It's clear that both Carrey and Howard are approaching the upcoming movie with care because of that, though. In addition to Carrey's previous comments in a conversation with ComicBook , in which he shared that “Anything is possible in this world,” Ron Howard has now talked about the upcoming movie with People , sharing the mutual condition that he and Carrey both had before considering a return to Whoville. Check out Howard's comments below.

Sequels are notoriously difficult, especially when they're sequels that are only the second movie following what has become a cult classic decades later. Howard and Carrey are clearly aware of the potential pitfalls here, though, as Howard has confirmed that they're not moving forward unless they have something great. Speaking with People , he said, “I just have to caution everybody that Jim and I aren't gonna go forward unless we think we have a great script, and we don't even have a script right now…We have really good writers and an idea that I'm excited about that I think is very much in keeping with the spirit of Dr. Seuss, his blend of comedy and fantasy. So I'm very pleased with what we have to work with, but I don't wanna make any promises that it's happening because Jim and I are aligned on one thing: we're not gonna go forward unless we believe it has a chance to be great.”

If anything, that's fantastic news for fans of the original, even in light of the fact that Howard is saying the sequel isn't a guarantee if they can't get to a place where both Carrey and Howard feel that it has something “great” to offer. That's a reasonable bar, and this update is still a promising one, as it seems there is, at the very least, a solid idea on the table. Given that Howard confirmed there isn't a script yet, it's doubtful whether the 2028 release date fans are hoping for will really happen, but this nevertheless seems like a positive sign that a sequel to How the Grinch Stole Christmas is still coming, and it won't disappoint.

articles.title: Demon Slayer's Infinity Castle Future Faces a Major Problem
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Ufotable Demon Slayer faces a huge problem with the adaptation of the final arc. Ufotable released the first installment of the Infinity Castle trilogy last year across the globe, and it became the highest-grossing anime movie of all time. Thanks to the long-standing popularity of the franchise and the exceptional adaptation by Ufotable, the anime only […]
articles.content:
What follows is a series of intense battles filled with heart-wrenching moments. The first installment has already struck fans hard by killing off several beloved characters, and unfortunately, there’s much more to come. Last year, following the Hashira Training Arc finale, Ufotable announced a trilogy adaptation of the final arc. At the time, it was widely assumed that both the Infinity Castle and Sunrise Countdown arcs would be included. However, after the release of the first part, the chances of the trilogy covering the entire final stretch now seem slim.

The final arc is divided into two parts: the Infinity Castle Arc and the Sunrise Countdown Arc. The Infinity Castle Arc alone spans 44 chapters, of which only 17 were adapted in the first installment. Despite the flashy animation and thrilling fight scenes, the fast pacing and exclusion of key scenes are impossible to overlook. The film ran for about 2 hours and 30 minutes, roughly the same length as the Infinity Train movie. But here’s the twist, the Infinity Train film adapted just 13 chapters within that same runtime, and few would argue it didn’t achieve far better pacing. If the latest film had tried to adapt its 17 chapters with the same level of detail, the runtime would have needed to stretch to nearly 3 hours, which simply isn’t practical.

The Infinity Castle Arc still has 27 chapters left to adapt in the upcoming installments, which is an ideal amount for a film. However, the Sunrise Countdown Arc spans 22 chapters, and it seems unlikely the trilogy will be able to squeeze this arc into the upcoming parts. This arc follows the surviving members of the Demon Slayer Corps as they put everything on the line to secure victory and defeat Muzan Kibutsuji. The full stretch of 22 chapters is more tragic than anything the series has shown before, ultimately concluding the story on a bittersweet note.

Following the groundbreaking success of its two films, Ufotable releasing a final anime film isn’t completely out of the question. However, the story might be better experienced through weekly episodes. The first installment of the trilogy is spectacular in every way, but it doesn’t change the fact that it would have worked far better in a TV season format . We see several characters scattered throughout the castle, fighting demons while also searching for Muzan.

The first part alone features three major battles, each following the other in quick succession, which reduces the suspense of wondering, “What’s going to happen next?” The upcoming installments will likely follow the same pattern, since many characters still haven’t had their turn to fight. As for the Sunrise Countdown Arc, it may work better than Infinity Castle as a film, but the studio would need to release at least two movies to adapt it fully. Perhaps a single anime season would be a better choice.

The Corps’ situation only worsens after the Infinity Castle Arc, as they now face the impossible challenge of defeating Muzan himself. Most members are already injured or exhausted, and with the demon progenitor’s only weakness being the sun, their task becomes even more daunting. The Sunrise Countdown Arc is packed with heart-wrenching moments and cliffhangers that will keep the audience hooked until the very end. The first installment of Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle is currently showing in theaters, so be sure to catch it on the big screen. You can also catch up with the anime on Crunchyroll and Netflix.

What are your expectations for the Sunrise Countdown Arc? Do you think Ufotable will continue making more movies, or will there finally be a TV show again? Share your thoughts in the comments below!

articles.title: Obsession Director Debunks the Biggest Theory About Who Was Possessing Nikki
articles.summary: IMAGE COURTESY OF FOCUS FEATURES Obsession, based around a powerhouse central performance by Inde Navarette as the possessed Nikki, is bringing in audiences who might not normally go to horror movies. There's one potential dealbreaker, however, even for audiences braced for jump scares, and that's the dead cat. Even though it's absolutely a prop, viewers who can suspend disbelief when […]
articles.content:
After all, Nikki at one point does her bodily functions on the floor, and so do cats, right? Cats can also be jealous of their owners giving attention to any other pets. Via Bloody Disgusting , director Curry Barker recently spoke with the YouTube show mojocore , and addressed this theory. Barker's answer was simple: “No.” It certainly doesn't seem likely that the ghost of a cat would feed its own body to its owner, but cats are weird.

Barker pointedly left a lot of open threads in Obsession , leaving vague the mechanics of how the One-Wish Willow works, and what the heck is up with their creepy customer service hotline that audibly appears to be operating out to some netherworld. In any potential sequel, which seems inevitable at this point, he may have to answer some of the questions we're left with. For now, though, part of the appeal of the movie is what it leaves to the imagination, which includes that ending… what exactly is going to happen to Nikki once the spell is broken ? If the One-Wish Willow abides by the rules of the Monkey's Paw on which it is clearly based, it could conceivably bring back the dead .

Barker says he used to keep up on every theory, but now there are more than he can keep track of, and he has a new movie to prepare — one that Seth Rogen insists is even better than Obsession . That one is called Anything but Ghosts , and is set to come out in May of next year. It's supposedly set in the same universe, but Barker now says there's just a small Easter egg, and he regrets mentioning it. Between then and now, though, Obsession is doing the awards circuit rounds, hoping to potentially score some acting nods for Navarette, in a genre that isn't often respected by awards bodies. There have been significant exceptions, however — if Kathy Bates can win an Oscar for Misery , and Anthony Hopkins for The Silence of the Lambs , well, another terrifying, complex antagonist with mood swings has a shot. Figures drawn from Indian mythology are headed for the streets of a stylized modern-day Mumbai in “ Bombay Eternal ,” an animated neo-noir crime fantasy from “ Rana Naidu ” producer Locomotive Global and AI-native film company Studio Blo , which have released a first teaser.

The project is planned as a feature film for eventual theatrical release in international markets, and the story will unfold across multiple parts. The partners are building it as a franchise from the outset and want the kind of worldwide reach achieved by “Ne Zha,” “Arcane,” “KPop Demon Hunters” and the “Spider-Verse” films. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Oscar Predictions: Production Design — Could Something as Innovative and Cool as 'Backrooms' Find Love? The story borrows characters and tales from Indian mythology and drops them into an original present-day setting where crime, magic and mystery mix with themes of redemption. The filmmakers have played freely with familiar archetypes, recasting them in a more modern story designed to be accessible worldwide. The teaser gives a first look at some of the main characters and locations, and shows off a visual style that pairs the bustle of the city with an animation approach that crosses genres.

Locomotive Global's slate also includes a Tamil-language horror film with Trisha Krishnan .

“The world of ‘Bombay Eternal' has been in the making for more than two decades. What began as an idea set in Manhattan has evolved considerably, but the core ambition has remained the same: to take characters and ideas inspired by our mythology and place them in a contemporary world in a way that feels cinematic, unexpected and globally accessible. Our partnership with Studio Blo is about finding the right creative and production ecosystem to finally realize that vision,” said Sunder Aaron, Locomotive Global's founder and CEO. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Studio Blo, which recently set an international series with “Elizabeth” director Shekhar Kapur , was co-founded by Dipankar Mukherjee, a filmmaker who also works as a creative technologist. The company has devised a look for the film that the team calls “painterly cinematic,” setting illustrated, painting-like foreground elements against deep, film-style environments. It is also contributing its in-house technology, production pipelines and global tech partnerships.

Over the past year, teams from both companies have worked out how the film will look and sound. Recruits include U.K.-based musicians and voice actors, along with production designers, cinematographers and artists drawn from Europe and the U.S.

“What drew us to this project was the opportunity to build a world rather than simply produce a film. The mythology gives us an incredibly rich foundation, but the visual language, characters and environments we are creating are distinctly our own,” said Mukherjee, who is also Studio Blo's CEO.

The partners said new production tools are being folded into the workflow to keep the film efficient and financially viable. They stressed, however, that craft, storytelling and design remain at the center of the project, along with the considerable human labor behind it.

More of the film will be revealed in stages. Much of its wider story world is being kept under wraps for now.

I was going to put “The Night Gwen Stacy Died” in this spot, but I couldn't ignore the Jade Giant. The Immortal Hulk is brilliant in every way , a comic that grabbed everyone's attention and didn't let go (even if the last issue is… certainly a comic we all read). Unlike a lot of other fans, I don't love The Immortal Hulk as fervently, but that doesn't mean I can deny the craft that went into this fantastic 50-issue series. Al Ewing and Joe Bennet, with multiple back-up artists, were able to take the ideas that had been budding across Hulk history and allow them to grow into what is easily the best Marvel horror comic ever.

The Immortal Hulk was amazing because it changed everything you knew about the Hulk, but it did it by using all of the building blocks you already knew about. Ewing was able to take the history of the character and add to it beautifully while always still staying true to the characters and events we already knew. Sure, it made Hulk power scalers more insufferable than ever, but it's the perfect example of everything you could want a modern Hulk story to be.

Stan Lee and Jack Kirby are Marvel's two greatest creators, known for breathing new life into the superhero in the Silver Age, starting with their best collaboration, Fantastic Four (Vol. 1). The two worked together on the book for 102 issues (and six annuals), creating the bedrock of the Marvel Universe. There are some brilliant stories from their time together across the Silver Age, but their best, the one that shows off what they each did so well, is Fantastic Four (Vol. 1) #48-50. Titled “The Galactus Trilogy”, it introduced the world to Galactus and the Silver Surfer.

Stan Lee was able to capture the panic of the end of the world, all while showing us the resolve of the heroes to save the day. Kirby loved creating massive cosmic gods like Galactus and is able to capture the grandeur of a being like the World-Devourer. The action has that Kirby energy and the Silver Surfer is the perfect fusion of Kirby and Lee's skills. It's a wonderful combination of big stakes sci-fi and human-scale tragedy. It's everything that you could want from Kirby and Lee, a true masterpiece that stands tall above the rest.

Daredevil has had some fantastic runs over the decades , and it all started with writer/artist Frank Miller. Miller took the character who used to basically just be blind Spider-Man and made him into something new. Miller's Matt Murdock lived in a hard world and had to be harder, all while still trying to keep some part of him human. Miller excelled at the hard-boiled crime stories during his run, making the threat of the Kingpin even greater than ever. However, his finest moment with ol'Hornhead came after his run ended when he returned to the book with “Year One” collaborator David Mazzucchelli for Daredevil (Vol. 1) #237-233.

This is the classic “Born Again”, where former Daredevil girlfriend Karen Page, now a heroin-addicted porn star (Miller certainly had… issues with women), sold his identity to the Kingpin. This led to Matt Murdock's life to be systemically dismantled, his nemesis destroying everything he held dear. However, Murdock is able to teach the Kingpin a lesson – that a man with nothing left to lose is a man without fear. Miller and Mazzucchelli created a masterpiece with this story, the perfect superhero crime thriller. Others have tried to match it, but none have gotten close.

Stan Lee gets a lot of praise that he doesn't deserve, but that doesn't mean he deserves no praise. Lee is an adroit writer when he wants to be and the best example of this is Silver Surfer: Parable . This two-issue miniseries teamed the master of the Marvel Universe with French icon Jean “Mobius” Giraurd for a story that saw the Silver Surfer have to step up to save the Earth again from the World-Devourer Galactus. However, there are some who use the coming of the giant to take power of their own, leading some to stand against the Sentinel of the Spaceways.

Lee often said that he enjoyed writing Silver Surfer more than any other character and if you ever read this book, you'll see why. Lee's Surfer is a philosopher from beyond the stars, trying to find the heart of humanity under all the cynicism of the modern world. Mobius is, as always, flawless. His pages bring Lee's words to life, bringing emotion to the spectacle in a way that no other artist could. This book is an example of two greats at their finest and I feel bad for the self-proclaimed Marvel Zombie that hasn't read this masterpiece.

“The Dark Phoenix Saga” is the X-Men's finest moment and in my opinion, the finest moment in Marvel history. Chris Claremont and John Byrne had been building up this story since their time on the book started, telling the story of the Phoenix coming to Earth and how it affected the lives of Jean Grey and the X-Men. This story would see it all come to a head, as the Hellfire Club captured her, the mental manipulations of Mastermind bringing out her dark side and leading to the birth of the Dark Phoenix. The X-Men now have to not only save the universe from her, but her from herself.

The reason why Uncanny X-Men #129-138 is so beloved is one word – emotion. Claremont is able to capture the emotions of the story perfectly. All of the rage, the sorrow, the resolve, the contrition, and those final heartbreaking moments of love come through beautifully because of Claremont's prose. Byrne's art is able to bring it all to life on the page, all while giving readers the kind of action and detail they'd come to expect from him. This story is, in a word, perfect.

What Marvel stories do you think belong among the best of all-time? Do you think I got any of these wrong? Leave a comment in the comment section below.

articles.title: Marvel Already Proved the Biggest Doomsday Complaint Is BS, And They Did It Eight Years Ago
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel With Avengers: Doomsday now just about a month away, the talk about both the hype and the disappointment heading into it has grown louder. There's obviously a lot of excitement for the first true appearance of Dr. Doom, the return of Wanda Maximoff, and seeing the Fantastic Four, the new Avengers, and many other heroes […]
articles.content:
In a lot of ways, that's an understandable feeling because of how up and down things have been in the MCU in general. We have had characters like the Eternals, She-Hulk, Moon Knight, and Shang-Chi, who appeared in one project and mostly disappeared outside of it . That makes the universe feel nowhere near as connected as it once was. Add in the inconsistent qualities of the franchise as a whole and you can see why people are concerned. However, the MCU has actually done something similar in the past and it ended up working out fine, so maybe it's not as worrisome as some believe.

The biggest complaint that faces Avengers: Doomsday for most people is that the build to Doom has been lackluster. We have yet to actually see Doom outside of the trailer. There haven't even been all that many scenes teasing the character. So far, Doom has only appeared on the big screen in the post-credits scene of The Fantastic Four: First Steps when he shows up to seemingly kidnap Franklin Richards. Those who went to see Avengers: Endgame Encore heard him arrive to take the Hulk, likely to join his cabal. Most recently, Doom appeared in VisionQuest to resurrect Wanda Maximoff, adding to the excitement for the film.

That is just three small scenes and nobody else has talked about him, as most characters don't even know he exists yet. That makes it feel like the audience is going into Avengers: Doomsday blind. We don't even know what his ultimate plan is or even what his motivation is outside of things that the Russo Brothers have brought up . When Thanos was the incoming big bad of the MCU, we at least understood that the Infinity Stones were in his sights, even if we didn't know about his motivations for wanting them.

Some of this stems from the pivot the MCU made from Kang the Conqueror. The franchise was clearly building him up with appearances in Loki and Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania , but they changed course for a few reasons. Jonathan Majors' arrest played the biggest part, but it also didn't help that the character wasn't getting rave reviews outside of his first appearance in the Season 1 finale of Loki . That made things a bit more disjointed than the MCU probably wanted. However, a lackluster build for a major villain is nothing new for the franchise.

The argument about Doom's build makes sense on paper, yet it shows that people forgot about Thanos' setup. The MCU didn't do a lot to build him up either . He had a quick cameo in The Avengers and then had a solid little appearance in Guardians of the Galaxy . His next cameo in Avengers: Age of Ultron didn't make much sense, as he talked about “doing it himself” with the Infinity Stones, seemingly disappointed in Ultron's efforts even though he had nothing to do with Ultron. That's all we got of him until Avengers: Infinity War .

That's a bit more than what we've had from Doom, yet it is pretty similar. We knew who the villain was and only a few characters knew he existed before Avengers: Infinity War . That 2018 film did a lot of heavy lifting as it established who Thanos is and how imposing he is early on. People mostly remember how great Thanos was as a villain because of Avengers: Infinity War , not because of how he was set up beforehand. Making him the protagonist of this movie worked expertly and there's a chance Avengers: Doomsday does something similar.

With such a vast number of characters on the hero side of things, it will be difficult to fully focus on most of them. The Russo Brothers have noted that Yelena will act as the heart of the film, but making Doom into more of the main character would allow him to succeed the way Thanos did. Regardless of the actual outcome of the film's quality, the MCU has proven that not giving the big villain a ton of build-up is actually okay. Their track record shows that Avengers: Doomsday should be alright.

How do you feel about Doom's build-up entering the upcoming blockbuster? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Why Prince Harry And Meghan Markle May Have Made Those US Holiday Plans
articles.summary: Going home for the holidays can get complicated.
articles.content:
Prince Harry , Meghan Markle and their two kids, Archie and Lilibet, have been adapting to a completely new life in the U.K. these past few months. However, some recent reports claim the family may already be getting ready to head back to Southern California to spend Christmas this year. That leads to the question: Why aren’t they allegedly starting new traditions across the pond?

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle spent their first two Christmas holidays with the Royal Family at Sandringham Estate. When that time of year rolled around in 2019, they had already formally separated from the Royal Family and appeared in a candid documentary interview where Harry said he and Prince Williams were "on different paths." So in 2019, they decided to spend the holidays privately in Canada with a nine-month-old Archie. And, in March 2020, they stepped away from being senior royals.

It's also worth taking into account that Meghan Markle and her mother have been reportedly leaning on each other following Markle’s father facing allegations of possessing child sexual abuse material. Thomas Markle Sr. was arrested by federal agents on November 6 and could serve prison time.
